parts.text:
12 A uniform rod is attached by a hinge at one end to a wall. The other end of the rod is supported
by a wire so that the rod is horizontal and in equilibrium.
wire
wall
hinge
rod
Which arrow shows the direction of the force on the rod from the hinge?
A
B
C
D

hints: Look at the wire in the diagram: it runs from the end of the rod up and to the left to the wall, so its tension on the rod pulls up and to the left.
For horizontal equilibrium the vector sum of horizontal forces must be zero, so the hinge must supply a force component opposite to the horizontal component from the wire.
Take moments about the hinge: the upward pull of the wire supports only about half the weight, so the hinge must also push upward on the rod.
walkthrough: Identify the three forces on the rod: weight $W$ down at the centre, tension $T$ along the wire from the rod end toward the upper wall fixing, and hinge force $H$ at the left end.
Resolve the tension: because the wire slopes up to the left, $T$ has an upward vertical component $T_y$ and a leftward horizontal component $T_x$.
Apply horizontal equilibrium: sum of $F_x = 0$, so $H_x - T_x = 0$. Hence $H_x = T_x$ to the right.
Apply moments about the hinge: $T_y \times L = W \times L/2$, so $T_y = W/2$ upward. This is less than $W$.
Apply vertical equilibrium: sum of $F_y = 0$, so $H_y + T_y - W = 0$, giving $H_y = W/2$ upward.
Combine $H_x$ to the right and $H_y$ upward: the hinge force points up and to the right, diagonally. This is option D.

A.explanation: A purely vertical force has no horizontal component to balance the leftward horizontal component of the wire tension.

B.explanation: A downward force cannot help support the downward weight of the rod when the wire already pulls upward.

C.explanation: An up-and-left force would add to the leftward pull of the wire, so horizontal forces on the rod could not balance.

D.explanation: An up-and-right force provides a rightward component to balance the leftward wire pull and an upward component to help balance the weight.
